differences.what: massing: a stone front two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard, 10.4 m across from the pavilion's north corner (x 160 px) to the corner bay's south edge (x 905 px), the cornice's top at y 357 px
differences.how: T-3155: the 1911 sheet's 10.47 x 17.46 m front block on K01, the principal floor 1.8 m, storeys 3.75 and 3.7 m, a K02 limestone front; the render's north corner on x 160 and its cornice within 5 px

differences.what: the recessed strip in shadow north of the pavilion (x 105-160 px), the north stack rising behind it
differences.how: T-3155: the sheet's stair projection on the north flank as a K08 pavilion 0.86 m behind the front; it renders on those pixels

differences.what: the door in the pavilion's south half (x 288-393 px) up a stoop, the window column south of it (x 495-577 px) on both storeys, the barred basement light under it
differences.how: T-3155: the door at v 3.36, the column at v 6.1, K01's area light under it

differences.what: the one-storey corner bay at the south-west corner (x 600-845 px), its north cheek canted with one light, two narrow lights in its front, barred basement lights under them, a stone balcony of pierced panels on its deck
differences.how: T-3155: a K08 projection 2.08 m wide and 1.2 m out with a 1.4 m canted left cheek, flush with the south flank, under K08's stone balcony with one row of pierced panels

differences.what: the gabled dormer in the mansard over the window column (x 470-600 px)
differences.how: T-3155: a gabled dormer at 6.1 m on the street face

differences.what: the pavilion: the photograph's is about 4.0 m wide (x 160-445 px) with the door in its south half; the build's is 2.2 m wide, 0.3 m in from the north corner and clear of the door, because K01 cannot cut a door through a projection; so the attic storey over it stands about 0.5-0.7 m north of the print's

the pavilion's attic storey: a stone wall carried up past the main cornice to its own eave at y 205 px (11.6 m), two paired lights in it (x 178-302 px, y 248-390 px), under its steep roof; the build's steep hipped crown starts at the main eave, so the paired lights and their wall are missing and the roof starts 2.4 m lower (its apex within 0.4 m of the print's)
differences.how: T-3156: the pavilion carried up a 2.4 m attic storey past the main cornice, the main eave stopping at its cheeks, a mullioned and transomed pair of lights in it (1.5 m clear, 9.25-11.0 m over grade), and K01's hipped crown raised onto its wall head (mansard.crown.attic_m 2.35): the crown's eave and apex render within about 0.3 m of the print's heights

differences.what: the pavilion's own dentil band at the second storey's head (y 440-470 px), lower than the main cornice; the build carries the main cornice across the pavilion
the door's pedimented hood on carved brackets (x 245-430 px, y 615-700 px) and the transom with the house number
the stoop's stone newels and cheek walls and the basement doorway under the landing
the narrow light over the door's south jamb (x 388-416 px, about 0.4 m wide): built at the storey's 1.1 m sash width
the corner bay's south edge renders about 40 px (0.5 m) south of the print's
differences.how: the bay's 1.2 m projection read through a camera fitted on the main plane; under a visitor's notice at the street

differences.what: the north stack stands about 0.8 m south of the print's (x 145-190 px): K01 stands a stack inside the main footprint and the print's rises from the stair projection
the mansard's cresting, the dormer's finial and the pavilion roof's cross finial (K01's deck cresting cannot stand on a mansard that carries a crown, k01_mansard_deck.resolve)
the leaded upper lights of the principal-storey windows and the bay's lights
differences.how: glazing pattern inside the sash, not read at the street's distance

differences.what: the stone's colour and tone: the print is monochrome and very light; the build's K02 Lemont limestone is buff, after the 1973 landmarks report's 'yellow limestone'
the street fence, the walk and the parkway's stone posts
differences.how: outside the building record; the boundary is not built on this house yet

differences.what: which front stood in 1904: the photographs are undated and show Joseph Sears's house; he sold it to Mrs. Grace Murray Meeker in March 1902 with fifteen rooms (Inter Ocean, 28 March 1902), and in 1915 it had twenty-one, 'extensively remodeled' after the purchase (Chicago Tribune, 1 May 1915), Arthur Heun's remodel (Chicagology); the 1911 sheet, drawing a one-storey projection north of the front's centre and no corner bay, is the remodelled house. Whether the remodel came before 1 July 1904 is not known (T-3156): the build follows the photographs (L-k01-1815-sears-1893)
the main cornice: the print's is a deep bracketed one, a row of large stone consoles under a moulded crown (y 360-430 px); the build carries K10's moulded stone cornice with no consoles
the stone shoulders either side of the attic storey (y 285-330 px), where the pavilion's 4 m block stops under the narrower attic
the low coping and the two square posts flanking the walk
differences.how: T-3206 lays K11's 0.25 m stone coping with 0.9 m posts either side of a 1.8 m opening and the K14 walk through it

differences.what: the posts' places along the lot line
differences.how: through the camera the print's posts stand at s 1.96-2.22 and 3.83-4.10; they are laid 0.2-0.45 m off, at the stopping rule's edge (T-3153)

differences.what: a low iron fence set back on the north side
differences.how: the print shows a low railing behind the coping north of the walk that no record explains; not built

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
